about: Reviewed starting inputs for the font-gvar target. The first byte picks the font's shape: 1 to 3 axes (its value modulo 3), long loca offsets (bit 2), long gvar offsets (bit 3), short horizontal metrics for half the glyphs (bit 4), side bearings that differ from the outlines' left edges (bit 5). The next 48 bytes choose 16 glyphs (empty, simple, composite, nested composites) and their tuple variations; every following 4 bytes (up to four times) choose one location (bytes 1 to 3: an axis at its minimum, default, maximum or a fraction between, by the value modulo 4). The font is built with 16 and 128 glyphs and 8 times the shared tuples.

seeds.why: one axis, no locations: only the default and the corners
two axes with four locations: corners, the default and fractions
three axes, so tuples peak on several axes at once
short horizontal metrics and side bearings away from the outlines' left edges
bytes that give most glyphs three tuples (choice byte 4 modulo 5) with shared peaks and intermediate regions
deltas scaled by 5 into words (bytes divisible by 11) and wide contours with word coordinates
only a choice byte: everything from zeros
